plan.p0: Treat each uniform block as a cell and preserve separator lines. In any cell row, if two equal non-background colors enclose background cells, fill the enclosed cells with that color. This changes the observed bottom row from 1,6,1,9 to 1,1,1,9. It assumes filling is strictly horizontal and requires matching endpoints.
plan.p1: Preserve the grid scaffold, then fill the rectangular bounding box of repeated same-colored marker cells, replacing background cells inside it. The two 1-cells in the observed bottom row have a one-cell horizontal box, producing the shown change. Unlike p0, this assumes markers can also define vertical or two-dimensional rectangles.
plan.p2: Interpret the cells as short symbolic motifs and complete a symmetric three-cell pattern: when the first and third cells match and the middle is background, copy that color into the middle. Thus 1,6,1 becomes 1,1,1 while 9 remains unchanged. This assumes only exact local three-cell symmetry matters, not arbitrary enclosed gaps.
plan.p3: For each row containing non-background markers, find the interval from the first to last marker and fill internal background cells with the most frequent marker color in that interval. The observed markers are 1,1,9, so the internal 6 becomes 1. This differs by using row-wise majority rather than endpoint equality.
